statements.t: “We believe 2027 will be an important year for cema-cel and the field, with upcoming ALPHA3 data expected to provide important insights into the potential for CAR T to be integrated into existing practice patterns, earlier in the course of a patient’s disease and closer to where they receive care.

At the same time, our ALLO-329 data set to be released next week will begin to address an equally important question in autoimmune disease: whether we can deliver meaningful clinical benefit with less reliance on chemotherapy-based conditioning.
Both programs reflect our conviction that the future of CAR T will be shaped not only by what these therapies can do, but by how we make them more accessible and practical for patients.”
The Company continues to anticipate its next clinical update in mid-2027, with trial enrollment expected to be completed by year-end 2027.
ALLO-329 is a next-generation, dual-targeting anti-CD19/CD70 AlloCAR T product incorporating the Company’s proprietary Dagger® technology.
Based on its cash, cash equivalents, and investments as of September 30, 2026, the Company continues to project its cash runway into 2029.
The listen-only webcast will be made available on the Company's website at www.allogene.com under the Investors tab in the News and Events section.
Following the live audio webcast, a replay will be available on the Company's website for approximately 30 days.

risks.t: patient enrollment and trial execution risks, including delays in enrollment
